ai.title: MoE Routing Strategies Explained: Top-K, Expert-Choice, Sigmoid Gating and Dynamic Routing (2026 Guide)
ai.brief: Every Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model repeats one decision for every token: which experts should process it. That decision belongs to the router. MoE routing strategies shape quality, load balance and serving cost in every major open model. This guide explains the 7 routing strategies used in production, and the models that use each one. TL;DR Size: Routers choose from 8 experts (Mixtral) to 384 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro), activating 1 to 8 per token. Runs on: Routing cost shows up in multi-GPU expert parallelism, where each choice becomes all-to-all network traffic. Performance: Sigmoid scoring with aux-loss-free bias balancing is the dominant 2026 recipe for frontier open MoE models. 04 at 1B, with lower perplexity. Worst: Expert choice leaks future tokens in causal models; one test showed a roughly 10% abnormal loss drop. Bottom line: Best thing: bias-based balancing adds no interfering gradients. Worst thing: no router removes the need for serving-time load fixes.

sec.title: Attackers Exploit Third-Party Provider to Raid French Bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
sec.brief: S. S. S. S. 3M set-top boxes into proxy servers French cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was hit by a cyberattack that let attackers make fraudulent transactions of up to $133 million, forcing it to suspend certain systems. Crédit Mutuel Arkéa is a major French cooperative banking and insurance group headquartered in Brest, Brittany, France. The bank says the attacker used its own account to send transactions to other banking organizations, and that customer assets weren’t affected. ” Reuters states .
